cells.tense: This is being written now, with the pen still moving across the page.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: In this one thing that's starting, give someone a real piece of help with it, all the way to done — their part, not yours — and stop there for today.
cells.core:
Something concrete is in your hands, new enough that the shape of it isn't settled. Fairness here isn't judged from outside; it's the thing staying even while it takes form, and it stays even because you're inside it, holding your end without carrying anyone else's.

What holds this is giving where it's needed and letting the help land: a real piece of it, finished, handed to someone it actually serves. Not the help you'd pick for them — the help their part needs. Give it that way and the arrangement holds level while the thing is still growing. The proportion comes from the help meeting the need, not from a tally kept after.
cells.sheetLine: The thing starts fair when your help goes where it's needed.
cells.verb: beginning a concrete thing — the first piece of it held in hand
cells.place: at the table where what each person gives and gets is being weighed, in this unfinished thing

cells.tense: Tomorrow arrives already braced — a future that can't be written in, only feared.
cells.act: take in the whole rainbow of what you feel
cells.ask: Before the next move you've already planned, take in the whole of what you feel about this — every colour, none skipped — then act, slowly.
cells.core:
You're pushing at something that's barely begun, already holding a picture of how it has to come out. The picture is doing the steering, and the steering is outrunning the thing itself — decisions made against a future you haven't met. What's real is what the people in it feel, and that part gets skipped.

Pause before the next move and take the whole thing in. Not the version that fits the plan — the actual mix, all of it at once. What you haven't let yourself feel has been running the show. Take it in fully, then move, and the move will be yours rather than the picture's.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed some time behind you.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: In the one place the balance looks wrong, set every part of it out together — what's been put in, what's come back — so you're not looking at it in pieces.
cells.core:
In this unfinished thing, the balance you can't feel isn't hidden — you just haven't looked at the whole of it together. What you've kept in separate rooms stays out of proportion. You aren't failing at fairness; you're working from a piece of the picture.

Set every part of it out at once, plain as a table: what's been put in, what's come back, in what form. Don't judge while you look — just look until nothing is in the dark. Seeing it all together settles the proportion, and you can act from the whole. Until then, no amount of effort would have told you which way was even.
cells.sheetLine: The whole picture is the missing piece, not the effort.

cells.tense: You are already writing this and don't have hold of the pen.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Look at the whole thing once before you touch it — the people, the shares, what you're about to do — and adjust from what you see, if you adjust at all.
cells.core:
An uneven patch shows up in a shared thing and gets evened out before anyone else notices — nothing said, nobody thanked, the proportions quietly back where they were. Somebody in this is doing that, and if you ask them, they'll tell you the thing just runs. Small corrections, made while nobody watches.

Before the next one, stop. Look at the whole of it — who's given, who's taken, what you're about to do — and only then move. If you still move, fine; nothing else changes. What shifts is that it's yours now, done in daylight rather than reflex. That's the whole difference, and you can make it in a second.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that I can locate this person's specific situation at all — in particular for Too Little, that anything specifically ended or was left behind; the record only says the capacity is under-expressed, not why. A reader could reasonably say 'that's not what's happening, nothing ended, I just don't see the equity yet' — the Too Little cell keeps its language on what the person cannot see or act on rather than asserting a loss, and the ask (see the whole picture, nothing hidden) survives no matter what the history is. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line that names their past door or claims I know what is out of proportion; there is none in the cells. The four acts are: Support 'share your strength where it is needed' (about people, so another may be part of the act); Completion 'take in the whole rainbow of what you feel' (the person's own, no one else needed); Clarity 'lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once' (the person's own); Clarity again for Unacknowledged, 'see it whole, with nothing hidden' — the same medicine, done nearer the act itself, since the authorship returns to the simpler form.
